title: Session-store UX + quick PRD sketch (personal notes)
content:
Goal: quick, informal sketch of a session-store feature for the hosted API to make short-term context cheap and UX-friendly. Personal notes/brain dump. Not a final PRD — rough user stories, tradeoffs, experiments, and a parking lot.

Background: customers keep asking for cheaper ways to maintain short-lived convo state and reuse compute across requests without forcing them to re-send long context on every API call. We already have prefix caching and KV cache at runtime but it's not exposed as a first-class user primitive.

Core idea: session-store is a managed, per-customer (or per-api-key) ephemeral KV of token-prefixes + embeddings that apps can pin and read via API. Primary use cases: conversational session resumption, few-shot example caching, search result context reuse, and cross-step tool state.

High-level properties (rough):
- Scoped by project/api-key/session-id.
- TTL defaults (e.g., 30m, 6h) configurable per session.
- Two storage modes: "prefix" (raw tokens or token-ids, used for direct prefixing/prefix-cache hit) and "semantic" (small embeddings + metadata for retrieval to construct prompts).
- Limits: per-account total active sessions and per-session size caps to control cost.
- Opt-in or explicit write: app must call sessions.append or sessions.put; read via sessions.peek or sessions.fetch for constructing prompt.

User stories (short):
- As a chat app, I want to append the last 3 user messages to the session so subsequent messages are cheaper and latency lower. Acceptance: tokens on subsequent inference calls are reduced; billing shows cache-hit reduction.
- As a document QA tool, I want to cache top-3 retrieved passages embeddings per session for 10m so repeated follow-ups reuse retrieval. Acceptance: embedding calls decline when cached, and relevance degrades within acceptable threshold.
- As a data-sensitive customer, I want sessions to be disabled for my org OR have automatic redaction hooks. Acceptance: sessions comply with KMS/HSM encryption and opt-out flag works.

API sketch (informal):
- POST /v1/sessions (create) -> returns session_id, ttl
- POST /v1/sessions/{id}/append { type: prefix|semantic, payload } -> 200
- GET /v1/sessions/{id}/fetch?mode=prefix|semantic&max_tokens=512 -> returns payloads, size_hint
- DELETE /v1/sessions/{id}
- Headers: X-Project, Authorization (api_key), optionally X-Session-Policy for write-mode

Instrumentation & UX:
- Console: per-session table (session id, created_at, last_seen, size, hit-rate). Quick toggle to materialize session into prompt builder.
- Metrics: session-hit-rate, avg-saved-tokens, cost-savings-estimate per client, number of sessions per api_key.
- Devflow: SDK helper (js/python) that wraps calls to append before send, and auto-fetch to assemble prompt.

Open implementation questions / tradeoffs:
- Storage model: in-memory redis-like hot store vs durable scalable store. Hot store for low latency but more cost; fallback to S3-backed segments for cold. Hybrid approach likely.
- Consistency: eventual vs strongly consistent for append/fetch. Append-order matters for prefix mode. Might implement append-ordered log with last-N retention.
- Size representation: store token-ids vs raw text. Token-ids smaller but ties to tokenizer-version; need migration story when model/tokenizer changes.
- Security/legal: if sessions stored for hosted API, ensure opt-out and ability to purge. Also retention logs for audits.
- Cost model: bill per-put (storage) and per-access (reads), or bake into inference pricing with visible discounts when hit-rate high. Need finance input.

Experiments to run (MVP):
- Internal test: enable in dev environment for 3 low-latency customers (search demo, chat demo, multi-step tool). Measure tokens saved and extra infra cost over 2 weeks.
- A/B: default OFF for new customers; opt-in for early adopters with dashboard. Measure retention and latency.
- Tokenization test: trial storing token-ids + tokenizer version tag; test with model upgrades.

Acceptance criteria for MVP:
- API available with append/fetch/delete
- SDKs wrap common flows and reduce avg request tokens by >= 25% in at least 2 apps
- Basic console visibility + per-session metrics
- Security: purge + org opt-out + KMS-encrypted storage for sessions

Parking lot / nice-to-have:
- Auto-eviction LRU across sessions to keep cost bounded
- Merging sessions across devices (conflict resolution rules)
- Prompt templates pinned to sessions (server-side templates)
- Built-in reranking of semantic cache candidates before constructing prompt
- Automatic summarization of long sessions into compressed prefix every N tokens

Immediate next steps (for me):
- Sync with Marco (infra) on cost estimates and possible infra architecture (redis cluster vs memtier + S3). Add JIRA task.
- Draft a minimal open API spec for internal review (include schema for semantic entry).
- Quick mock in console: table + fetch flow, hand off to Aisha for UX polish.
- Slack thread: #product-session-store (start), invite Liam and Marco.

Unresolved questions to bring to roadmap meeting:
- Pricing approach and whether session storage is a paid add-on or included for premium tiers.
- Long-term interaction with dedicated/private offerings: for private deployments we probably expose a toggle to store sessions on-customer infra only.

Notes-to-self: keep this personal doc short; move to shared drive after first sync. Save a copy to CONFLUENCE-SESSION-IDEAS-2025 after initial feedback.

--Priya
(rough, iterative)
